cards.headline: Florida rejects $18 billion Meta settlement, becomes sole state to pursue independent lawsuit over youth safety
cards.teaser: Florida has become the only state in the nation to reject its share of a nearly $18 billion settlement with Meta over allegations the company knowingly harmed children's mental hea
cards.body:
Florida has become the only state in the nation to reject its share of a nearly $18 billion settlement with Meta over allegations the company knowingly harmed children's mental health with addictive platforms. Attorney General James Uthmeier announced the state will proceed with its own lawsuit against the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, calling the national settlement insufficient and a slap on the wrist for the trillion-dollar corporation.

 The 48-state agreement requires Meta to pay nearly $18 billion over 10 years to participating states and territories for youth online safety programs. Uthmeier described the payouts as peanuts compared to the profound harms Meta's profit-driven addictive features inflicted on children. He argued the total settlement amounts to roughly one month of revenue for Meta and fails to create a real deterrent.

 The settlement mandates new safety features on Meta's platforms, including a two-hour daily time limit for teenage users, blocking platform access between midnight and 6 a.m., and muting all notifications during school hours. Meta has committed to paying 70% of the settlement upfront, with the remaining 30% contingent on competitors like YouTube and TikTok agreeing to similar restrictions. North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson said Meta told parents everywhere that their top concern was the safety of their children when it was actually making money.

 Florida's independent case against Meta is just beginning. Uthmeier has pledged that Florida will hold Meta accountable, stating that corporations like Meta will never learn a lesson if they do not incur real costs for breaking the law.
